name: pitch-panel
promise: Put a startup idea in front of six seats (CTO, CMO, COO, PM, CFO, devil's advocate), then get a verdict and one cheap test.

installBy.note: Then run /pitch-panel:grill and describe your idea. Updates arrive through the marketplace.
Run in your project, then tell your agent to follow PITCH-PANEL.md for your idea. You will not get automatic updates this way.

preview.title: One seat's block
preview.note: Illustrative output for a made-up idea (a subscription box of left-handed kitchen tools). Every number is tagged.
preview.body:
## CFO   Vote: Back it if   Score: 3/5

Strongest objection: at $39 a box with 40% product cost and about $9 shipping, contribution is roughly $14 a box [assumption]; a $25 acquisition cost pays back in two boxes only if monthly churn stays under 15% [assumption].
Why it matters: most subscription boxes lose half their buyers in three months, which would erase the margin.
What would change my mind: a pre-order cohort where 40% re-order the second box.
Question I would ask in the room: what happens to cash if only half the expected boxes sell?
One number I would want: landed cost per box from two real suppliers.

preview.title: The devil's advocate
preview.note: Same made-up idea. It speaks last and must name something the other five did not.
preview.body:
## Devil's advocate   Catastrophic risk

Scenario: one large marketplace lists a cheaper left-handed range and takes the search traffic the whole plan depends on.
Trigger: the marketplace sees the category selling.
Likelihood: medium [assumption]
Earliest warning sign: competing listings appearing under the same search terms.
Cheapest hedge: build an email list of buyers from day one, so demand does not depend on one platform's search.

preview.title: The verdict
preview.note: Same made-up idea. The test and its pass bar are stated before it is run.
preview.body:
## Verdict: Go if   (score 20/30)

Conditions: 1. Buyers pay for a one-off box, not only a subscription (PM). 2. Landed cost leaves 40% margin after shipping (CFO). 3. Ten buyers reached for under $5 each (CMO).
Kill triggers: fewer than 5 of 20 interviewees will pay; second-box re-order under 25%.
This week's test: a one-page priced pre-order for a three-item box, shown to 200 left-handed people. Pass bar: 12 pre-orders.
Not checked: competitors' real prices, supplier minimums.

I am not an investor and this is not a prediction; talk to real buyers before you decide.

reads: The idea you describe, and any files or links you point it at
writes: Nothing, unless you ask it to save the result to docs/pitch-panel.md
access.network: None from the kit: it has no scripts and no hooks. If your agent has web search it may use it only when you allow it, and the skill says to name the pages it opened.

limits: Not investors and not a forecast: the verdict is a structured argument, not a prediction.
Only as good as the facts you give it; anything unsourced is tagged as an assumption.
The seats are played by one model, so they share its blind spots. Talk to real buyers before you decide.
Deep mode (separate sub-agents for each seat) costs many times more tokens than the default single pass.
Not affiliated with any television programme or brand.
